checks: The predecessor supplies the central and reflected axis census, exactly three canonical direction classes, strict outside saturation for the positive choices, and weight one third in each class. At fixed class, every matching positive guard is captured and no negative guard is captured.

On paired copies of a single guard the centroids and boundary length measures coincide and the field takes opposite constant values. Their contributions to D and each centered moment J_u cancel. There are 3L positive guards, each paid one third of its perimeter.

For φ=Φ or Φ+ε the support speed on each of the three unit facet normals is φ, by dividing scale velocity by the regular triangle inradius. Opposite base weights agree in every representation of zero, so the Minkowski averages of the guards have the same support gaps to the moving central triangle as before. Positivity and the exact integer base census hold for both signs of small t.

The area derivative is −D and the centered quadratic-moment numerator derivative is −J_u. Quotient differentiation of the square root at old Γ(u)=1 gives (D−J_u)/(2M). For the outward ramp, fixed affine margin has derivative of q equal to −q times the norm derivative, so the raw loss is the captured boundary term plus A times that norm derivative. The piecewise linear ramp is Lipschitz and its kink hyperplanes are area-null. Dividing by mass and differentiating produces the sign −βD in M times the normalized loss.

The full fixed-menu response is linear in the field. For Φ+ε the numerator tends to the positive captured boundary loss and the denominator is ε times the positive total boundary length. This is a fixed-menu result as in original §§1–2, distinct from its §3 global descent consequence.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use its finite reflected-axis family with σ=1/4, regular T, and the stated positive width regime. Its canonical positive selections have strict saturation and form a balanced menu with weight 1/3 per canonical direction.

overlap.comparison: The accepted source-facet moment law uses an optimizing separator and a homothetic positive-source distribution. Its covariance term has a related centered quadratic moment, but its hypotheses and conclusion give no signed reflected-guard cancellation or divergent response ratio.

readability: The symbols P_D and r_T are recoverable as the common guard perimeter and the inradius of T, respectively. The original note makes these definitions explicit. W is the probability-weighted ramp profile of the fixed menu.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The selected balanced menu has exact positive signed response with zero volume and covariance derivatives. The first-order ratio diverges along the positively priced constant perturbation.
